findings.reason: as written a worker either reports a phantom figure change caused by ingested traffic or cannot pass the gate; the done-when needs the before/after comparison pinned to one frozen input (a fixture index and price history, or one snapshot re-rendered), which is a change to the node's instruction on line 890.
findings.text: §24's done-when measures a render "against the live index" and then asserts "The month cost and every period's cost in the JSON are identical before and after"; the ingest loop writes new rows every 60 s, so the month token total (and every open period's) grows between the before-render and the after-render and the cost necessarily moves — the assertion is unsatisfiable on a live index and can only hold against a frozen input, which the node's own brief does not name

findings.reason: naming the index query as removable points the profile-and-fix node at a cost that cannot be removed without contradicting "without changing any figure"; narrowing it to the hoistable history scan keeps the node off a fix that would alter the pricing rule §18 set.
findings.text: §24 attributes the +106 s to "work repeated once per hour or per segment that could be done once per period, such as reading the price history or querying the index", but §18 (line 799) prices each segment on that segment's own `partitioned_total`, so the per-segment index queries in `watch.py:_span` -> `telemetry_index.partitioned_total` are inherent to the segmentation and hoisting them to one query per period would change the figures §24 also requires be held — only the per-segment full-history scan in `provider_prices.provider_median_in_force`/`rate_in_force` is genuinely hoistable repeated work
